ecosystem.notes: No filing reports App Store volume, so measure is null and the figure sits in studies[]. The study was paid for by Apple ('Support for this study was provided by Apple'), published June 2026 and covers calendar 2025; Apple's fiscal 2026 ran from September 28, 2025 to September 26, 2026, so the periods overlap by about three months only. Its Table 1 total is $1,437B ('more than $1.4 trillion'). About 79% of it ($1,137B) is physical goods and services bought through apps (general retail, travel, food delivery and pickup, grocery, ride hailing and digital payment, the last $16B), on which Apple takes no commission, and about 10% ($151B) is in-app advertising, so it is not App Store sales; digital goods and services are $149B (10%). The study says its estimates 'may not be directly comparable to previous reports'. The 90% no-commission claim is kept with value null (it is a percentage). The study does not state developer earnings or payouts. platformRevenue is null because Apple's FY2026 10-K does not break out App Store revenue: it is inside Services net sales, and the 10-K says 'the Company accounts for all third-party application–related sales on a net basis by recognizing in Services net sales only the commission it retains' (FY2026 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000026/aapl-20260926.htm).

footprint.notes: Apple's only state-by-state publication is the Job Creation page (apple.com/job-creation), which is still live but dated: its footnote says direct employees are as of December 31, 2016 and the page was updated May 2017. It is nine years older than the FY2026 (Sep 2026) edition year, and no newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24; the page itself is unchanged and still says 'Page updated May 2017'); the February 2025 $500 billion release and the August 2025 $600 billion American Manufacturing Program release name states but give no per-state figures. The page's 'App Store ecosystem jobs' per state are an estimate by the Progressive Policy Institute (Michael Mandel), not an Apple count, so they are left out. The 51 state cards sum to 77,822 Apple employees, against the page's headline of 80,000 U.S. employees, versus approximately 167,000 worldwide full-time equivalent employees as of September 26, 2026 in the FY2026 10-K. In the earlier research pass the retail store list (apple.com/retail/storelist) named stores by state and country but stated no counts (not re-checked in this refresh), so no store counts by country were recorded, and the 10-K gives no geographic breakdown of employees or facilities. Sites come from the FY2026 10-K (Cupertino headquarters), the Job Creation page (2017 descriptions) and the February 24, 2025 newsroom release.

Payroll: the FY2026 10-K discloses no total staff cost (no salaries, compensation-and-benefits or employee-cost line), so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median is used.
